321: Warm-start tuning requires a compatible objective metric. Changing from precision to recall requires a fresh search, whose elapsed time can be reduced through parallel trials.
The objective changes from precision to recall, so the previous trials cannot be reused through the stated warm-start mechanism even though the new parameter ranges overlap.
Training checkpoints preserve a model's training state. They do not convert an earlier precision-based hyperparameter search into a recall-based one.
Reusing a random seed supports reproducibility, not faster execution of a different tuning objective.

Running multiple training trials concurrently reduces the new search's wall-clock duration within the available capacity. Very high parallelism can reduce Bayesian search adaptivity, so it should be configured deliberately.
322: TF-IDF combines a term's frequency within a document with its rarity across the document collection, highlighting words that distinguish that document.
Topic counts summarize latent themes rather than directly measuring how distinctive a queried word is in a particular article.

Length-aware term frequency captures local prominence, while inverse document frequency downweights words common across many articles. Their product supplies the requested document-specific relevance weight.
Similarity to a title embedding measures semantic proximity to the title, not how frequently and distinctively the queried word occurs in the full article.
Raw term counts with stop-word removal ignore corpus-wide frequency and can favor long articles or common non-stop words. They omit the inverse-document-frequency component.
323: High availability requires independent failure domains and sufficient healthy capacity. Multiple subnets within one Availability Zone do not provide multi-AZ resilience or prove a five-minute RTO.
A VPC cannot span AWS Regions. Multi-Region deployment requires separate regional resources and a routing or failover design.
Autoscaling adjusts capacity in response to demand or metrics. It does not alone establish the required failure-domain placement or recovery guarantee.

Multiple instances across at least two Availability Zones are the likely intended design. As written, two subnets in the same second AZ do not clearly specify that design, and the recovery target remains unverified.
Backups support recovery but do not provide a ready serving endpoint or a tested five-minute failover. Cross-Region recovery would need additional deployment and routing automation.
324: Textract extracts printed document text and structured fields, while Comprehend custom classification assigns document categories from text.
A custom OCR model and custom classifier both require training or packaging, hosting, and maintenance that the managed services avoid.
Comprehend is suitable for classification, but operating PaddleOCR in SageMaker adds a custom OCR serving workflow unnecessarily.
Textract is appropriate, but Rekognition is an image-analysis service rather than the direct text-document classifier for the extracted content.
Textract can extract the required text or fields, and Comprehend can classify the resulting content using a trained custom category model, minimizing custom model operations.
325: For rare fraud, recall measures how much fraud is caught, while F1 balances that coverage with the precision of fraud alerts.
Specificity measures correctly rejected legitimate transactions. It does not directly measure the fraction of fraud captured.
False positive rate measures how often legitimate transactions are flagged. It matters operationally but does not directly reward finding actual fraud.
With only 2% fraud, a classifier that always predicts legitimate reaches 98% accuracy while detecting no fraud at all.
F1 combines precision and recall, discouraging a solution that achieves high recall only by flagging almost every transaction.
True positive rate is recall: the share of actual fraud detected. Maximizing it directly supports capturing as many fraudulent transactions as possible.
326: Versioned S3 buckets with Cross-Region Replication maintain object versions in another Region without manually provisioning storage capacity.

S3 scales with the object collection, versioning preserves object history, and CRR creates accessible replicas in another Region. Replication is asynchronous, so newly uploaded objects are not instantly present in both Regions.
EBS volumes require capacity management and are not an object-versioning repository. Snapshots must be restored into volumes before normal file access.
Regional EFS storage spans Availability Zones within one Region, not multiple Regions as required by the question.
Volume Gateway exposes block volumes and cloud-backed snapshots. It does not provide the requested automatic multi-Region object repository and version access.
327: Production variants allow traffic-split evaluation behind the same SageMaker endpoint name, preserving the calling application's API integration.
A new endpoint and ALB proxy design add infrastructure and routing work. SageMaker endpoints are not direct ALB target groups in the proposed simple arrangement.
Adding the new model as a production variant preserves the existing endpoint and lets the team gradually adjust its traffic share while comparing production metrics.
Batch Transform performs offline scoring and does not distribute requests to models behind a real-time endpoint.
An NLB-based proxy arrangement adds resources and does not offer the built-in model-variant traffic controls needed here.
328: DeepAR handles explicitly marked missing target observations, avoiding the need to invent target values before training.
Regression imputation adds a separate modeling step and can introduce misleading target patterns, especially when most values are absent.

Encode missing target values using DeepAR's supported JSON representation, such as null or the string NaN. A bare NaN token is not standard JSON, and extensive missingness still limits available training evidence.
Forward filling assumes the target remains constant through each gap, which can create artificial flat segments in the forecast history.
Mean imputation suppresses variation and can distort temporal patterns. Native missing-target handling requires less development and avoids this assumption.
329: Textract signature analysis returns signature blocks with confidence and page information. Those are detection scores, not proof of legal signature validity.

AnalyzeDocument with the SIGNATURES feature returns detected signature blocks and their confidence values. The application can associate those blocks with pages; multipage asynchronous documents require the corresponding start/get analysis workflow.
Prediction is not the Textract API action used for signature analysis.
StartDocumentAnalysis begins an asynchronous job but does not itself return the completed signature results. SIGNATURES must be requested and the result retrieved afterward.
GetDocumentAnalysis retrieves an already-started asynchronous job's output. Calling it alone does not initiate signature detection.
330: This workflow needs localization of each corrosion region, supervised severity classification, and additional variation for the extremely rare positive images.
Object detection can locate multiple corrosion regions in one photo, producing regions that can be evaluated separately for maintenance severity.
Generic Rekognition label detection is not trained for the company's specific corrosion severity and maintenance categories. A custom task-specific model is needed.
K-means finds unlabeled similarity groups. Those clusters do not automatically correspond to the engineers' immediate, scheduled, and no-action labels.

XGBoost can classify severity from engineered measurements or embeddings extracted from detected regions and paired with engineer labels. It does not directly replace visual feature extraction from raw photos.
Label-preserving augmentation increases variation among the scarce corrosion examples. Apply it only to training data and keep related image variants out of validation and test sets.
Augmenting the already overwhelming non-corrosion class increases the imbalance and does not supply the missing diversity of corrosion examples.
331: Containerized offline scoring can scale through AWS Batch, with Spot capacity reducing cost for retryable jobs and shared high-throughput storage supplying the input.
Reserved capacity requires a commitment and does not supply the flexible Spot pricing benefit. Instance-store data is also local and ephemeral rather than a durable shared dataset.

Batch can schedule the ECR container across Spot instances, and FSx for Lustre can provide shared high-throughput access to S3-backed data. Jobs must tolerate retries; actual cost still depends on instance and file-system utilization.
A SageMaker notebook is not a scalable batch scheduler, and EC2 Reserved Instances are not configured as the notebook purchasing mechanism described.
SageMaker notebook instances do not use the proposed EC2 Spot purchasing workflow. EFS alone does not provide scalable job scheduling.
332: Hyperband combines parallel configuration exploration with successive resource allocation, stopping weak trials and giving promising trials more training budget.
Grid search evaluates a fixed combination set and does not inherently reallocate training resources based on intermediate performance.
Random search samples configurations efficiently but does not by itself provide the requested successive elimination and resource-promotion strategy.
Bayesian optimization uses previous results to choose configurations, but the specific requirement to stop weak trials and promote stronger ones is the defining fit for Hyperband.
Hyperband evaluates many configurations with limited initial resources, eliminates underperformers, and increases the budget for survivors, reducing wasted training computation.
333: SageMaker Model Registry organizes successive versions of a model into a model group and records their metadata and approval state.
An ECR repository stores container images. A separate repository per model does not supply model-package versioning, evaluation metadata, or approval workflows.
ECR tags identify container images, not the complete model lifecycle record. The team would need to build the missing model-registry behavior.
Registering model versions in a model group uses the registry's native versioning and lifecycle management without a custom catalog.
Tags can add searchable metadata, but they do not replace the model group's native version relationship. A custom tag-based version convention adds work.
334: SageMaker managed warm pools retain provisioned training infrastructure for reuse by compatible subsequent jobs, reducing repeated infrastructure startup time.
Managed Spot Training targets compute cost and may wait for or lose Spot capacity. It does not preserve an immediately reusable warm training environment.

Warm pools reuse the retained instances for matching jobs within the keep-alive period, avoiding repeated infrastructure provisioning between consecutive experiments. Retained capacity remains billable.
Training Compiler optimizes supported model computation during training. It does not retain infrastructure between jobs or remove the provisioning stage.
SMDDP distributes training computation across workers. It targets training throughput rather than the infrastructure startup delay before a job begins.
335: A manual deployment gate registers a model as PendingManualApproval and changes its registry status only after an authorized reviewer approves it.
Experiments organizes training runs and comparisons. It does not itself enforce a model-package approval gate for production deployment.
Lineage tracks relationships among data, jobs, and artifacts. Recording approval-related entities does not enforce the deployment decision.
Model Monitor detects quality or drift issues. It does not manage the registry's manual approval transition.

Pipelines and the registry can support the gate when a reviewer uses the SDK to mark the registered version Approved and deployment checks that status. Automatically approving every registration would defeat the manual-review requirement.
336: Bias monitoring compares configured bias metrics on current data with a reference baseline; an application can submit an on-demand Clarify processing job.

Lambda can start the Clarify job and return while managed processing runs. The job needs appropriate facets, labels or predictions, and a baseline to evaluate drift; Clarify is no longer open to new customers.
Pulling the model-monitor-analyzer image is not a bias-analysis workflow, and that analyzer primarily supplies data-quality statistics and constraints.
Glue Data Quality checks dataset quality rules. It does not directly calculate the model fairness metrics and baseline comparisons supplied by Clarify.
A notebook can run custom comparisons, but requires interactive or separately automated code execution rather than a simple application-triggered managed job.
337: Lake Formation can coordinate a governed data lake and ingestion workflows, while Spark can also combine S3 and JDBC data. The question does not state a constraint that uniquely excludes either approach.

Kinesis Data Streams ingests event records. It does not by itself extract and join the existing S3 datasets and on-premises database tables.
DynamoDB stores key-value and document data. It does not automatically aggregate the heterogeneous existing sources into a training dataset.

Lake Formation's Glue-backed ingestion workflows can bring database data into a governed S3 lake. This supports the source's intended answer, but the wording also permits the Spark alternative, so the key is not finalized.
338: Data Wrangler offers anomaly-detection analysis together with visual inspection in the data-preparation workflow.
Athena can execute custom SQL analyses, but the query service alone does not perform the requested automatic anomaly detection and visualization.
Spectrum queries external data; it does not automatically supply an anomaly detector. A separate analysis and visualization integration would be needed.
Data Wrangler's anomaly-detection visualization can identify unusual records and display their distribution without building a separate detector and dashboard pipeline.
Batch schedules compute jobs but contains no built-in detector for this dataset. The team would need to implement the analysis and integrate its output with QuickSight.
339: Categorical features often need an appropriate numeric encoding before they can be consumed by the chosen ML algorithm.
Glue can encode categories, but configuring an ETL transformation requires more work than selecting the relevant built-in Data Wrangler transform for this preparation task.
Discretizing numeric values can be useful in some models, but it does not encode the existing categorical features and can discard useful numeric detail.

Data Wrangler provides categorical-encoding transforms through a visual flow, reducing custom preparation work. Choose the encoding based on cardinality and whether the categories have a meaningful order.
Changing numeric features into categories does not address the unencoded categorical inputs. Such binning needs a separate modeling justification rather than being a general accuracy improvement.
340: Data Wrangler's Balance Data transform can oversample an underrepresented class as part of a repeatable preparation flow.
Athena can count classes and inspect patterns, but the proposed manual adjustment adds custom work instead of using a dedicated balancing transform.
Selecting a training algorithm in Studio does not itself resample the dataset. Class weighting can be useful, but it is not the specified preprocessing operation.
DataBrew has general preparation and sampling operations, but this option does not identify an equivalent dedicated minority-class balancing operation. Data Wrangler exposes that task directly.
The Balance Data operation applies configured oversampling without a custom resampling implementation. Split the data first and balance only the training partition to avoid leakage.
